policy: Third-party educational context is not an independently validated trading edge. No external research is a substitute for the protected assessment or actual historical market data.

records.title: What is a stock, and what does the market do?
records.objective: Explain the difference between a share of ownership, a stock quote, and a request to buy or sell.
records.claim: An ownership share, a displayed bid/ask quote, a last completed trade and a new broker order represent different things. Displayed or last-trade prices cannot guarantee a new fill.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: 100 shares out of 1,000,000 outstanding is (100 / 1,000,000) × 100 = 0.01% of the shares. At a hypothetical $10/share, simple market capitalization is 1,000,000 × $10 = $10,000,000; this is not company cash or a sale valuation.
records.counterexample: A screen shows a prior last trade of $10.00; a new buy order may face a different ask, limited size, delays and price changes. Do not infer a $10.00 fill.
records.transfer: Explain what a current quote, earlier last trade, issuer identity, order instructions and execution record each establish for a new fictional security. Choose NO TRADE when executable information is absent.
records.limit: SEC sources establish general order and share concepts, not a verified HBLT issuer, real quote, guaranteed order fill or actual trade history.

sources.claim: Bid/ask quotations are distinct from opening/closing historical observations.
Quotes apply to specific available share quantities; later order execution prices can change.
Market capitalization equals per-share price times outstanding shares.

records.title: How to read a five-minute candlestick
records.objective: Label open, high, low and close, calculate real body versus full range, and recognize an undefined range percentage.
records.claim: A candlestick represents open, high, low and close over a defined interval. Its body spans open and close, while its shadows extend to high and low; it does not disclose the intrabar event order.
records.counterexample: When high equals low, the range denominator is zero, so the body percentage is undefined; never force it to 0% or 100%. A bullish body alone is not a reliable forecast.
records.transfer: For an original fictional bearish candle O=24.00, H=24.50, L=22.50, C=23.00, calculate body=$1.00, range=$2.00 and body %=50%. State one reason for NO TRADE without future bars.
records.limit: StockCharts is a technical education publisher rather than a regulator. These original numerical OHLC examples are synthetic and do not verify an exchange print, future direction, intrabar chronology or historical chart license.

sources.claim: Definition of candle real body, shadows, high/low and OHLC construction.
Distinction between historical daily OHLC and contemporaneous bid/ask stock quotes.

records.title: Claims, catalysts and what was actually known
records.objective: Separate an original source and its publication time from a social repost, marketing claim or later price observation.
records.claim: SEC EDGAR is an appropriate primary record for issuer filing statements, but filing period, EDGAR acceptance and actual public dissemination are separate timing facts. An after-pause repost or price move cannot justify an earlier decision.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: a claim is posted at 08:10 ET; the learner pauses at 08:12; a newsletter at 08:17 and screenshot at 08:21 are later than the pause and cannot be prior evidence. A claimed 08:03 original document still needs authenticated identity and availability.
records.calculation: At an 08:12 ET pause: 08:17 is 5 minutes later; 08:21 is 9 minutes later. Both are inadmissible as earlier decision evidence.
records.counterexample: An SEC filing accepted at 08:03 does not establish that a given browser or trader could read its contents at 08:03. SEC notes typical public posting delays of 1–3 minutes and possible longer delays; independently verify availability.
records.transfer: Use a real publicly accessible 8-K to record issuer name, form type, reporting period, acceptance time and separately available publication/dissemination evidence; state what cannot be proven at a selected historical pause.
records.limit: A filing validates only what it disclosed, not whether any historical stock move was caused by it. No case price or trader-knowledge chronology is verified in this fictional lesson.

sources.claim: EDGAR search and distinctions among Form 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K.
EDGAR acceptance timestamp is not the same as verified web-publication time; usual 1–3-minute lag may grow.

records.title: Make a watchlist, not a list of trade signals
records.objective: Organize a small research watchlist with stated purpose, dated evidence, uncertainty and an explicit removal/no-trade rule.
records.claim: A research watchlist is an organizational method, not an order or verified trading signal. Primary issuer/SEC records can establish particular dated disclosures, but cannot by themselves establish liquidity, execution conditions or future returns.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: label GUSIM as SIMULATED STUDY with original exercise provenance; label Candidate A as INVESTIGATE with a dated issuer disclosure and unknown liquidity; reject Candidate B if it has only an unattributed repost. None is a buy recommendation.
records.calculation: No numeric calculation is required by this objective. The independent operation is a three-way provenance classification: verified dated source, original fictional exercise, or unverified claim.
records.counterexample: A candidate trending on social media or ranking first in a scanner is not a verified issuer disclosure or proof of a tradable setup. Even a genuine issuer disclosure does not establish executable order depth.
records.transfer: Build a fictional watchlist with purpose, source URL/issuer, source date, last reviewed, evidence status, uncertainty, next verification action and a specific removal/NO TRADE rule for every row.
records.limit: SEC guidance supports research and source verification, not the profitability, completeness or regulatory approval of this original watchlist framework.

sources.claim: Investment research and checking company disclosures are part of due diligence.
Search for issuer filings via SEC EDGAR to establish documented disclosures.

records.title: Plan risk, choose NO TRADE and review your work
records.objective: Use a hypothetical share-risk calculation, explain execution uncertainty and write a defensible independent NO TRADE decision.
records.claim: Risk-per-share arithmetic estimates a planned exposure from an assumed entry and stop reference. SEC order guidance establishes that a stop may trigger a market order with a price different from its trigger; a limit order may remain unfilled.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: assumed entry $10.00, stop reference $9.80 and planned risk budget $20. Risk/share=$0.20; floor(20/0.20)=100 shares. Notional exposure=100 × $10.00=$1,000. This is not a guaranteed $20 maximum loss.
records.counterexample: If a hypothetical exit executes at $9.60 rather than the $9.80 stop reference, price-only loss on 100 shares is ($10−$9.60)×100=$40 before fees, not $20. If liquidity inputs are missing, choose NO TRADE.
records.transfer: Recalculate the hypothetical risk using an entry of $10.00, stop reference $9.75 and $20 planned budget (80 shares before fees/slippage). State why a limit order may not fill and why no market order should be sent from a teaching exercise.
records.limit: These are user-independent fictional arithmetic and SEC general education. Actual fills, gaps, fees, slippage, buying power, short availability and broker-specific stop handling remain unverified.

sources.claim: Market, limit and stop order definitions; market/stop prices can differ from expectations and limit fills are not guaranteed.
Stop price is a trigger rather than a guaranteed execution price; brokerage order handling differs.
